lessons.title: The Cell: Life’s Building Block
lessons.body:
Every living thing is made of **cells**. The *cell theory* says that all living things are made of cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and new cells come only from existing cells.

## Two kinds of cells
- **Prokaryotic** cells (bacteria and archaea) have no nucleus. Their DNA floats in the cytoplasm.
- **Eukaryotic** cells (plants, animals, fungi, protists) keep their DNA inside a **nucleus**.

## Organelles that show up in questions
| Organelle | Job |
|---|---|
| Mitochondria | Make energy (ATP) through cellular respiration |
| Ribosome | Build proteins |
| Chloroplast | Photosynthesis (plants and algae only) |
| Cell wall | Rigid outer layer (plants use cellulose) |
| Golgi apparatus | Package and ship proteins |

**Quiz bowl tip:** clues often start with an obscure detail (like "cristae") and end with "powerhouse of the cell." Learn the early clues to buzz first.
keyFacts: Robert Hooke named “cells” in 1665 after looking at cork.
Mitochondria have folded inner membranes called cristae and make ATP.
Chloroplasts contain the green pigment chlorophyll.
Prokaryotes like bacteria have no nucleus.
Plant cell walls are made mostly of cellulose.

lessons.title: Reading the Periodic Table
lessons.body:
The **periodic table** arranges elements by **atomic number**, the number of protons in the nucleus. Dmitri **Mendeleev** published the first widely used version in 1869 and left gaps for elements not yet discovered, such as gallium.

## Rows and columns
- **Periods** are rows. Elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells.
- **Groups** are columns. Elements in the same group react in similar ways.

## Famous groups
- **Group 1, alkali metals** (lithium, sodium, potassium): very reactive, react with water.
- **Group 17, halogens** (fluorine, chlorine): very reactive nonmetals.
- **Group 18, noble gases** (helium, neon, argon): full outer shells, almost never react.

Element symbols that don’t match English names are a favorite clue: Na (sodium, from *natrium*), K (potassium), Fe (iron), Au (gold), Ag (silver), Pb (lead).
keyFacts: Mendeleev published his periodic table in 1869.
Noble gases (group 18) have full outer electron shells.
Au is gold, Ag is silver, Pb is lead, Fe is iron.
Hydrogen is element 1; helium is element 2.

tossups.question: The inner membrane of this organelle is folded into structures called cristae. This organelle has its own DNA, and it produces most of a cell’s ATP through cellular respiration. For 10 points, name this organelle called the “powerhouse of the cell.”

This scientist predicted the properties of “eka-aluminium,” which turned out to be gallium. Element 101 is named for him, and in 1869 he published a table arranging elements by atomic weight. For 10 points, name this Russian chemist who created the periodic table.

bonuses.leadin: Answer these questions about groups of the periodic table, for 10 points each.

parts.question: Name the group 18 elements, such as neon and argon, that have full outer electron shells and rarely react.
This group 1 metal, with symbol Na, reacts violently with water and combines with chlorine to make table salt.
Chlorine and fluorine belong to this group 17 family, whose name means “salt-former.”
